analysis.investment_thesis: CP PLUS operates in a growing surveillance market with a decent brand and clean debt (D/E 0.08), but at 105x P/E it is priced for perfection in a business with near-zero FCF and deeply questionable earnings quality. This is not a Damani buy at any price near current levels.
key_strengths: Strong promoter holding at 76.91% — well above my 55% floor, signals skin in the game
Virtually debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.08) with borrowings collapsing from ₹436 Cr to ₹128 Cr in FY25
Revenue CAGR of 20.2% over 5 years with EBITDA expanding from ₹62 Cr to ₹258 Cr — real operating scale-up
key_risks: Valuation is absurd for a Damani portfolio — P/E 105x vs my ceiling of 20x; even forward P/E of 61.7x is 3x too expensive
Earnings quality is deeply suspect — ₹259 Cr 'Other Income' in FY25 accounts for nearly 74% of ₹351 Cr net profit, yet OCF was only ₹27 Cr and FCF was ₹1 Cr
Structural moat is thin — CP PLUS competes directly with Hikvision and Dahua (its own distribution partner) in a commoditising surveillance hardware market
red_flags: Other Income exploded from -₹12 Cr (FY24) to +₹259 Cr (FY25) — this is not recurring operating profit; core EBIT-derived profit is ~₹92 Cr, below FY24 levels
Free cash flow is effectively zero (₹1 Cr in FY25) despite ₹351 Cr reported net profit — classic divergence that signals either working capital stress or non-cash income
Total assets doubled in one year (₹1,644 Cr → ₹3,373 Cr) and equity surged ₹1,163 Cr — a large capital event (likely IPO/QIP proceeds) is masking the underlying earnings trajectory
Operating CF was negative ₹180 Cr in FY24 — a business that consumes cash when growing is not a compounder in my book
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CP PLUS has built a recognisable brand in India's fast-growing security and surveillance segment, and the five-year revenue journey from ₹1,238 Cr to ₹3,112 Cr (20.2% CAGR) is respectable. Operating margins have expanded from 4.6% to 11.2%, and ROE of 20.9% looks attractive at first glance. But I always look at cash, not accounting profit — and the cash tells a very different story. FY25 FCF was ₹1 Cr on ₹351 Cr reported net profit. The ₹259 Cr Other Income in FY25 (versus -₹12 Cr in FY24) is almost certainly a one-time event tied to the balance sheet restructuring — total equity jumped ₹1,163 Cr in a single year. Strip that out and core earnings are closer to ₹90 Cr, implying a real P/E north of 290x. I built DMart by never paying above 20x for any business, and I never will.

The competitive dynamics also concern me. Surveillance hardware is a technology-driven, Chinese-dominated commodity business. CP PLUS distributes Dahua products alongside its own — the same manufacturer competes with its own distributor globally. That is not a moat; that is a dependency. Government and infrastructure contracts provide some revenue visibility, but margins will compress as AI-enabled cameras from Hikvision and Dahua flood the market at lower price points. The sector sits outside my circle of competence in consumer-facing, predictable demand businesses. At ₹2,264 per share and a market cap of ₹26,673 Cr, I see no margin of safety — I see a stock priced on narrative, not earnings. I will wait on the sidelines.
